evidence_class: Mocked in CI: rendered Pod manifests checked without a cluster, a cache store whose read only mount is simulated through the store's mount probe, and a local artifact directory replaced by a file to model lost shared storage. No NFS mount and no live rollout proof; the one live observation is the network reachability probe from a Pod on a swarm EC2 node in benchmark.wan.
interfaces: scripts.swarm_v2.kubernetes.storage.MountChecker().check(pod): refuses shared_runtime, unscoped_shared_write and operator_home with StorageRefused(message, reason); shared_runtime_mount_rejections_total() counts every reason
python -m scripts.swarm_v2.kubernetes.storage <pod.json>: exit 0 when the Pod passes, 1 with the refusal, an unreadable file or a non Pod document on stderr, 64 on usage errors
Pod policy mounts (docs/swarm-v2/schemas/pod-policy.json): seed, artifact and cache with a claim, host_path or nfs source; load_policy refuses repeated names or normalised paths

scripts.swarm_v2.kubernetes.spec.PodTemplate.render: seed and cache render read only, artifact renders writable with subPath set to the execution id; a Pod failing the checker is refused with reason storage; shared_runtime_mount_rejections_total() on the template
scripts.swarm_v2.cache.Store.read_only (default mounted_read_only, the statvfs read only flag of the nearest existing folder): attach on a read only store writes nothing, publish from it is refused

scripts.swarm_v2.artifacts.publication.publish(store, artifact_id, source) -> Publication(published|paused, ref, reason): the ArtifactStore is bound to its owner from a launch grant at construction; an OSError from the artifact backend pauses publication and leaves the attempt files untouched
scripts.swarm_v2.artifacts.publication.SWITCH (SWARM_ARTIFACT_PUBLISHING=off): pauses artifact publication alone, the attempt keeps its files; any other value publishes

python -m scripts.swarm_v2.artifacts.benchmark <folder> --sizes <MiB,...> --rounds N: put throughput per size through the artifact adapter in a fresh subfolder, then a loss probe on that subfolder (paused, source intact, published after restore); removes only its subfolder

remaining_limitations: The cloud to on-prem artifact throughput figure is not measured: swarm EC2 nodes carry no NFS client and no on-prem export admits their tailnet addresses (benchmark.wan); opening such an export waits on the operator
The node cache owner process that publishes seeds into the read only store is named in docs/swarm-v2/storage-policy.md, not built
Eviction on a store that attempts only read falls back to publish order
The checker is lexical; a node host path that is a symlink into a home passes, node layout and policy authors are trusted

benchmark.where: local WSL disk on the operator workstation, not the cloud to on-prem WAN path

loss.reason: artifact storage is unavailable (Not a directory)

wan.throughput: not measured; blocked by the gap below, not by the network

export_scope.source: declared exports in antoncore dev: automation/monitors/nfs-exports-check.sh EXPECTED_EXPORTS and automation/swarm-brain-storage/storage.vars; read from source, not from the live /etc/exports
export_scope.command: git show origin/dev:automation/monitors/nfs-exports-check.sh | grep -oE '^  "/mnt[^|]*\|[^ ]+ [^ (]+' | sed 's/|.* / admits /'; grep -oE '10\.10\.30\.[0-9]+/32' automation/swarm-brain-storage/storage.vars | sort -u
export_scope.gap: Every declared export admits only 10.10.30.0/24 or the on-prem node /32s (the first line of each multi-client export shown); swarm EC2 nodes register with tailnet 100.x addresses (kubectl node InternalIP 100.78.174.24 and 100.123.3.87), so none admits them

failure_evidence: tests/contracts/storage_layout/fixtures holds the smallest Pod for each refusal (shared-codex-home-pod, operator-home-pod, writable-node-cache-pod) beside safe-pod rendered from pod-policy-shared; the cases use no random seed
rollout_safety: SWARM_ARTIFACT_PUBLISHING=off disables only artifact publication; a pod policy without mounts keeps the qualified private Pod; the storage checker itself has no off switch
production_path: KubernetesTransport.apply_operation renders through PodTemplate and its storage checker; an operator home policy answers REFUSED with no create sent, a safe policy creates a Pod with a read only seed and cache and an artifact mount scoped to the execution id (tests.contracts.storage_layout.test_entrypoint)
authority: Publication scope comes from the registration the launch grant authorization returns; a store whose authorization answers with a seat or task label is refused with the ungranted error; the artifact subPath is the launch execution id, never a Pod label
data_safety: Authoritative: committed artifact objects and records, node cache seeds, attempt worktrees. Disposable: attempt private home and tmp volumes and the benchmark's own subfolder. Tested: rollback with publishing off leaves the artifact store byte for byte unchanged and a committed artifact verified; the benchmark leaves pre existing records in its mount unchanged
